name: Varnish File Purge
description: Sends PURGE/BAN requests directly to a Varnish server for a file's URL (and its image-style derivatives) whenever the file entity is inserted, updated, or deleted.
project_description:
The Varnish file purger is a Drupal project developed to address compatibility issues between the Varnish Purge and Purge File modules, especially in setups where files are served across multiple domains. In scenarios involving the file_replace module, those existing modules did not effectively handle file purging, leading to stale file caches being served by Varnish.

Unlike the Purge-framework modules it is compared to, varnish_file_purge does NOT depend on or use the purge framework, its queue, or its processors. It hooks file entity insert/update/delete and sends PURGE or BAN requests straight to a configured Varnish host over Guzzle, one request per configured domain (via a spoofed Host header), for the file's absolute URL. When the file is updated it only purges if the bytes actually changed (size, URI, or a sha256 content hash differ). Optionally it also purges the existing image-style derivatives of PNG/JPEG files.

Post-Installation: configure at /admin/config/development/varnish_file_purge. Settings: Varnish connection (scheme, host, port), the purge method (BAN or PURGE — prepare your VCL for the chosen verb), the comma-separated list of domains so the purge fires across every front/back-office host, a Debug toggle that logs each purged URL, and a Purge Image styles toggle.

Requires a functional Varnish set-up you can reach from the web server. Similar projects: Purge File (purge files across multiple domains) and Varnish purge (use Varnish as a CDN and purge caches).
